title: Static and Relative Positioning
ques: Explain the difference between **`position: static`** and **`position: relative`**. Write a CSS snippet showing how `relative` nudges an element without disturbing neighboring layout flow.
explanation: `static` is the browser default where elements flow naturally. `relative` allows shifting an element using offset coordinates without removing its footprint from normal document flow.

title: Absolute Positioning and Containing Blocks
ques: Explain how **`position: absolute`** interacts with the nearest positioned ancestor (`position: relative`). Write an example positioning a close button in the top-right corner of a card.
explanation: An absolutely positioned element is removed from normal flow and positioned relative to its closest non-static ancestor. If no positioned ancestor exists, it positions relative to the viewport (initial containing block).

title: Fixed Positioning for Persistent UI
ques: Demonstrate the use of **`position: fixed`** to build a floating 'Back to Top' button that stays pinned to the bottom-right of the viewport regardless of scrolling.
explanation: `position: fixed` removes the element from normal flow and anchors it relative to the browser viewport. It stays locked in position as the user scrolls.

title: Sticky Positioning for Section Headers
ques: Explain how **`position: sticky`** toggles between relative and fixed behaviors based on scroll offset. Write a CSS rule creating a sticky table header.
explanation: `position: sticky` behaves like `relative` until its containing element crosses a scroll threshold (e.g. `top: 0`), at which point it sticks in place until its parent container scrolls out of view.
